title: Slimline token slewing, retry-sculpting and lightweight stream handles (py/ts/go)
author: Priya Patel
description: Motivation: production workloads showed coordinated refresh spikes and increased tail latency when many clients attempted credential rotation at the same token-window boundary. This PR introduces three ergonomic, cross-language changes: 1) token slewing: a deterministic jittering layer on top of credential refresh that spreads refreshes across a configurable window to avoid thundering refresh storms; 2) retry-sculpting: a lightweight retry profile compiler that picks compact backoff shapes based on endpoint semantics (idempotent vs non-idempotent) and recent success/failure histograms; 3) slim stream handles: a reduced-allocation stream primitive for async iterables/pullstreams that minimizes buffer churn and exposes an ergonomic .pause/.resume surface for consumers. Scope and compatibility: changes are implemented in Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs and the polyglot connector glue in the redwood core. Default behaviors preserve existing semantics (token slewing is opt-in via SDK config flag slewing.window_ms; retry-sculpting uses conservative presets by default). The PR also bumps package versions to py-sdk v1.13.0, ts-sdk v2.7.0, go-sdk v1.8.2 and adds cross-SDK docs and examples. Checklist: - [x] Token slewing core algorithm with unit tests and integration test against mock auth server - [x] Retry-sculpting presets and small DSL + tests - [x] Slim stream handle implementation + examples in streaming-echo reference app - [x] Telemetry for refresh jitter, retry profile selection, and stream pause/resume events - [x] Cross-SDK parity tests and version bumps - [x] Docs and migration notes (README and examples) Changeset summary: commits include an auth shim in the transport layer that adds slewing jitter prior to refresh requests; a minimal retry-compiler that produces compact backoff profiles that are persisted per-client instance; and a new StreamHandle interface minimizing allocations and exposing pause/resume/close semantics with backpressure hints. Tests: unit + integration in CI; added a small load test harness that demonstrates 3.8x reduction in simultaneous refreshes under synthetic fanout compared to prior behavior and 6-12% improvement in 95th percentile generation latency for multi-tenant workloads under default batching. Migration notes: opt-in flag slewing.window_ms present in all SDKs; owners of SDK consumers should set it to 2000ms for initial ramp. Telemetry: metric names added: sdk.auth.slew.duration_ms, sdk.auth.slew.spread_pct, sdk.retry.profile_selected, sdk.stream.pause_count. Backwards compatibility: default semantics unchanged unless flag enabled. Rollout plan: feature flag gated on account tier; gradual rollout to hosted customers over 2 weeks. Related: ENG-2392 design doc (internal link) and SUP-501 customer report.

review_comments: Lars Müller: Could you add a short note on how slewing interacts with short-lived tokens? Concern about early refresh wasting work.
Priya Patel: Reply: slewing only delays the refresh trigger; we still check expiry and will do immediate refresh if token invalidated. Added unit tests for forced-revoke paths.
Evan Ruiz: CI flake on TS streaming example — observed race on resume(). Fixed by switching to microtask scheduling in the example.

release_notes: Add opt-in token slewing to spread credential refreshes, introduce retry-sculpting presets for compact backoff shapes, and expose a lightweight StreamHandle with pause/resume for lower allocation and better backpressure control. Cross-SDK parity and version bumps: py 1.13.0, ts 2.7.0, go 1.8.2. Opt-in: slewing.window_ms configurable; default off.
notes_for_maintainers: Monitor sdk.auth.slew.spread_pct and sdk.retry.profile_selected during rollout. If upstream customers report increased immediate refreshes, ensure slewing.window_ms not set below 500ms. Version bumps required aligned package publishing steps for py/ts/go.
